options.text: Applies the 'active' class only when isActive is truthy

questions.explanation: In the object syntax, each key is a class name toggled by the truthiness of its value — 'active' applies when isActive is truthy.

questions.prompt: If an element has both class="card" and :class="{ selected: isSelected }", what happens?

options.text: The dynamic class replaces the static one
They merge — 'card' is always applied, 'selected' when isSelected is truthy
Only the static class is used

questions.explanation: Static class and dynamic :class merge, so 'card' is always present and 'selected' is added conditionally.

questions.prompt: Which is a correct :style binding for a dynamic pixel font size?
questions.explanation: Style values are expressions, so you must include the unit: size + 'px'. Property names use camelCase (fontSize) or quoted kebab-case.

questions.prompt: Vue automatically adds vendor ______ to CSS properties that need them, so you write the standard property name. (one word)
questions.explanation: Vue auto-prefixes styles requiring vendor prefixes at runtime, so you don't have to write them manually.

questions.prompt: Which are valid ways to use :class? Select all that apply.

options.text: An object nested inside an array: :class="[base, { active: isActive }]"

questions.explanation: class binding supports object syntax, array syntax, and objects nested in arrays. A bare number is not a meaningful class binding.

questions.prompt: When should you prefer toggling a CSS class (:class) over inline :style?

options.text: Never — inline styles are always better
For reusable or themable styling; reserve :style for values genuinely derived from state

questions.explanation: Prefer :class for reusable/themable styles. Use :style for values computed from state, like a width percentage or a dynamic color.
